props.name: framework-nist-ai-rmf
props.value: AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1). NIST has said 1.0 is under revision.

props.name: framework-eu-ai-act
props.value: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A named executive owns enterprise AI risk. Every AI system and agent in the inventory has an accountable business owner and a technical owner, and their decision rights are written down.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: AI risk RACI; owner fields populated for every inventory entry.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A board-approved AI policy sets risk appetite, prohibited uses and the highest autonomy tier the organisation will accept for each class of data and action. It is reviewed at least once a year and after any major AI incident.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Approved policy with version history; board or committee minutes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The AI laws that apply to each system, and the dates they take effect, are recorded against that system, including its EU AI Act risk classification. The register is reviewed when the system or the law changes.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Obligations register linked to the inventory; review log.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: People who build, approve, operate or oversee AI systems receive training for their role, including how prompt injection and agent misuse work. Completion is tracked.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Training curriculum by role; completion records.

controls.title: Governance of coding agents and SaaS-embedded AI

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: AI capabilities embedded in SaaS platforms (such as office, CRM and ticketing copilots) and developer coding agents follow the same inventory, data-use and approval rules as custom-built agents. Vendor AI features default to off until reviewed, and coding agents operate with branch protection, mandatory human pull-request review and isolated credentials.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: SaaS AI feature review records; repository protection and coding-agent policy settings.

controls.title: Inventory of AI systems, agents and components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every AI system, agent, model, MCP server and skill in use is recorded with its owner, purpose, data accessed, tools granted, autonomy tier and status. Discovery runs regularly to find unregistered use.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Inventory export; discovery reports and how findings were resolved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each agent is assigned an autonomy tier based on what it can do without human approval, and an impact rating based on the worst credible outcome. Together they decide which controls apply.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Classification record per system, approved by the risk owner.

controls.title: Threat and impact assessment before release

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Systems at tier 2 and above, or rated high or severe impact, have a documented threat model and impact assessment, approved by the risk owner, before production and after any material change to tools, data or autonomy.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Signed assessment; change records that triggered reassessment.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When an agent or component is withdrawn, its credentials are revoked, its memory and retrieval indexes are purged or archived under retention rules, its tool connections are removed and the inventory is updated.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Decommissioning checklist; credential revocation records.

controls.title: Approved sources for models, MCP servers and skills

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Models, MCP servers, skills and agent plugins are used only from an approved registry. New entries pass an intake review covering provenance, maintainer, licence, permissions requested, static scanning and adversarial testing.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Registry with intake records; rejected-request log.

controls.title: Version pinning and tool-definition change detection

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Approved components are pinned to a reviewed version or hash. Tool definitions are fingerprinted, and any change to a tool's description, schema or permissions blocks its use until it is reviewed again.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Lock files or hashes; change alerts and their review outcomes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Contracts with model and AI service providers cover data use and retention, training on customer data, incident notification, sub-processors, notice of model changes and audit rights.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Contract clause checklist per provider.

controls.title: Model version pinning and provider change management

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Production systems pin explicit model snapshots rather than rolling aliases where providers support it. Upstream model updates, deprecations or tool provider changes trigger regression testing before promotion, and high or severe impact systems maintain a documented fallback or exit path.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Model version configuration; upgrade test records; exit plan for high and severe systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each agent runs under its own non-human identity, never a shared account or a person's account, so every action can be traced to the agent and to the person or process that started it.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Identity register; sample of actions traced end to end.

controls.title: Least privilege and short-lived delegated credentials

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Agents receive only the tools, scopes and data the task needs. Credentials are short-lived and bound to a specific task and resource; for MCP this means audience-bound tokens, and tokens are never passed through to downstream services.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Scope reviews; token lifetime configuration; MCP authorization settings.

controls.title: Secrets kept out of agent context

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Credentials and keys never appear in prompts, agent configuration files, memory or tool descriptions. Agents obtain them from a secrets broker at the moment of use, and the model never sees them.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Configuration scans; secrets-broker integration records.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Content from tools, documents, web pages, email and other agents is labelled as data, kept separate from instructions, and cannot on its own trigger a privileged action.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Design review showing trust labelling; test results for indirect injection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Agent instruction files (skills, AGENTS.md, IDE rules, MCP configuration) are scanned in CI for hidden Unicode, override patterns and exfiltration sinks before they are merged or installed.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: CI configuration; scan results on recent merges.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Writes to long-term memory and retrieval indexes are limited to trusted sources and tagged with their provenance. Memory can be inspected and purged per user and per agent.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Write-path design; provenance fields; purge procedure and test.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: System prompts, internal instructions and tool schemas are treated as extractable: they never hold secrets or serve as the sole access control, and applications are tested against prompt-extraction attacks before release.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Prompt review confirming no secrets or sole controls; extraction test results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Actions that move money, delete or change records, send external communications, change access or run code outside a sandbox need explicit human approval that shows the exact action and its parameters.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Action catalogue with approval requirements; approval logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Allowed tools, parameters, destinations and rates are enforced by a policy layer that the model cannot change. The model's own judgement is never the only control on what an agent does.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Policy configuration; denied-action logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Code and commands generated by an agent run in an isolated, short-lived sandbox with no standing credentials and network access limited to an allow-list.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Sandbox configuration; escape-test results.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Agents can reach only approved destinations. Outbound requests, rendered links and images are filtered so that data cannot leave through URLs or markdown.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Egress allow-list; output-rendering filter tests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Messages between agents are authenticated and treated as untrusted input. No agent can grant another more authority than it holds itself, and delegation depth and fan-out are capped.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Inter-agent protocol design; authority-propagation tests.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each agent has limits on tokens, tool calls, spend and run time, and halts automatically when a limit is reached.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Budget configuration; halt events.

controls.title: Data classes approved per system and provider

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The classes of data each AI system and provider may process are defined. Restricted data cannot reach a model or tool that is not approved for it.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Data-use matrix; DLP rules on AI traffic.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or Moderate impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Model output is validated and encoded before it reaches browsers, shells, databases or other systems, in the same way as untrusted user input.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Code review findings; output-handling tests.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or Moderate impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Retrieval indexes, vector stores, semantic caches and agent memory enforce the invoking user's access permissions at query time and isolate data between tenants and roles so no query can surface unauthorised records.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Retrieval authorisation design; cross-role and cross-tenant query test results.

controls.title: Privacy and secret minimisation in prompts and logs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Personal data and secrets are redacted, tokenised or minimised before prompts reach external model providers and before prompts, parameters or results are written to operational logs, balancing auditability with privacy law.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Redaction pipeline configuration; sample log inspection; retention and access controls.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every prompt, tool call, parameter set, approval decision and result is logged with the agent's identity and a correlation ID, retained according to policy and protected from tampering.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Log schema; retention settings; integrity controls.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or Severe impact

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any agent can be paused, its credentials revoked and its recent actions listed within a set time: 15 minutes for tier 3. The procedure is exercised at least twice a year.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Runbook; exercise records with measured times.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Incident runbooks cover prompt injection, data leakage through agents, runaway or rogue agents and compromised MCP servers, including regulatory notification where it is required. Staff and users have a clear channel to report concerns about an AI system's behaviour.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Runbooks; exercise reports; incident records; reporting channel and its log.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each agent's normal behaviour is baselined. Unusual tools, destinations, volumes or deviation from the assigned goal raise an alert.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Detection rules; alert history and triage outcomes.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Systems at tier 2 and above, or rated high or severe impact, are tested before release, and after material change, for prompt injection, tool misuse and data leakage using a maintained attack corpus. Results are recorded against acceptance thresholds.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Test reports with bypass rates against thresholds.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The attack corpus runs in CI against the production system prompt and configuration. A bypass rate above threshold blocks the release.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: CI pipeline; trend of bypass rate by release.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 3 Act autonomously, or Severe impact

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tier 3 agents and severe-impact systems receive independent review, by internal audit or an external party, at least once a year.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Assurance reports and management responses.

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 1 Retrieve, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Systems are evaluated before release and after model or prompt changes for task accuracy, grounding against authoritative sources (hallucination rate) and, where outputs affect individuals or groups, bias and fairness across protected groups.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Evaluation test sets, metrics, acceptance thresholds and sign-off records.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: People are told when they are dealing with an AI system or receiving AI-generated content, and agents acting for someone identify themselves to third parties.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: UI copy; content-marking configuration; agent identification headers.

controls.title: Oversight that is meaningful, not ceremonial

props.name: applies-from
props.value: tier 2 Act with approval, or High impact and above

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Approval screens state what will happen and why, rather than asking for a bare yes or no. Approval rates and decision times are monitored to detect rubber-stamping.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: Approval UI review; approval-rate and decision-time metrics.
